body_html:
Great post from Abby about our Mozilla Open Leaders IndieWeb and #OER Ghana project in Accra, Ghana. Please give it a read and then share our GoFundMe. History
I am on the Advisory Board to the Global Open Initiative Foundation in Accra, Ghana. Last year Southern Connectuct State University provided $200 seed money to pay for hosting costs for Sadik, a founder, and I  to start a club encouraging people to build personal websites and take control of their social stream.


Mozilla Open Leader Fellowship

After getting the program up and running Sadik and I were awarded a fellowship from Mozilla to develop the program and then train an additional ten leaders in Ghana to start clubs back on their campuses. The goal is  to create an Open Educational Resource network across Ghana.
https://foundation.mozilla.org/en/blog/indieweb-and-oer-ghana-open-leaders-x-program/

IndieWeb and OER Ghana | an Open Leaders X program Mozilla is a global nonprofit dedicated to keeping the Internet a global public resource that is open and accessible to all. foundation.mozilla.org

We are launching the 10 week program in February and will conclude with a two day Camp in Accra, Ghana.

We also have a massive network of experts across many disciplines to help members craft high quality teaching materials and running events: https://wiki.goifnetwork.org/Our_Mozilla_OLX_Volunteers


Sadik and I have also been busy working on curriculum, trainign guides, and support club leaders will need. The curriculum  https://wiki.goifnetwork.org/OER_Ghana:_Mozilla_Leaders_X_Training_Curriculum  is based off of a class I teach at Southern  https://edu106.jgregorymcverry.com/

Elm City Webmakers


A similar club is relaunching in New Haven called the Elm City Webmakers: http://elmcitywebmakers.com/. I used to run it on campus. This club will offer after school training for all ages, students, parents, grandparents. We begin on Monday! It is cosponsored by Concepts for Adaptive Learning and Junta.

Like the Ghana program anyone who shows up will get a free website. We will also have a free chat room and a wiki for students to share ideas.
We are currently applying for grants to secure free transportation for  Hamden and NHPS students.


Please Help
I applied for a social justice grant and a sabbatical to support this work but I unfortunately wasn't awarded either. Luckily Nate Angell  set up a fundraiser and will donate all the money to the Global Open Initiative. 

Can you share the link to the Mozilla post and to our fundraiser, GoFundMe,  across your networks?
